title.en: Spend detail on the features that join parts

summary: Model bosses, clips, seams, gaskets and joinery before adding surface ornament, because they explain how the object is made.
objective: Direct modelling effort towards the features that make an assembly legible and buildable.
applies_when: An object is presented as manufactured or built rather than sculpted.
A close viewing distance, cutaway or exploded view will show how parts meet.
An object looks like a smooth blob or like separate shapes floating next to each other.
example_prompts: Make the speaker housing look like two moulded shells that actually close.
Show how the timber frame joints carry the roof.
negative_signals: Distant background props where these features cannot be resolved.
Abstract or diagrammatic objects where construction is not the subject.
not_for: Distant background props where these features cannot be resolved.
Abstract or diagrammatic objects where construction is not the subject.

principles: Objects communicate manufacture through their junctions: a parting line, a screw boss, a lap joint or a welded seam says more about an object than another bevel on a flat face.
Junctions also carry consequence. A gasket implies a sealed volume, a clip implies a service opening, and a mortise implies a load path.
Detail spent where nothing joins is invisible work. Detail at a junction is read from a distance because it interrupts the silhouette and catches light differently.
Material follows the junction: the same joint in timber, aluminium and moulded polymer has different thickness, radius and tolerance.
implementation: List the junctions before the surfaces: what closes against what, what is fastened, what slides, what seals.
Give each junction its minimum expressive geometry, such as a recess, a lip, a fastener head or a visible fillet, sized for the intended viewing distance.
Match feature scale to the process you are implying: moulded parts get draft, radii and ejector marks; machined parts get chamfers and tool radii; timber gets shoulders and pegs.
Show clearance where parts move relative to each other, since a zero gap on a moving joint reads as a fused mass.
Only after these are in place, add ornament, wear and branding, which then have real edges to accumulate against.
observable_checks: Look along a junction at a grazing angle: parts that interpenetrate or float apart are visible there first.

Where the object claims to be serviceable, ask how each part would be removed and look for the fastener, clip or opening that allows it. A part with no such feature is not thereby impossible: welded, bonded, cast-in, moulded-in and sacrificial parts are ordinary, and the honest outcome is to say the part is not serviceable rather than to add a fastener that the design does not have.
Compare feature size against the implied process; a moulded shell with knife edges and no draft reads as an approximation.
Check that a cutaway or exploded view reveals internal features rather than empty shells.

creative_affordances: Fantasy and invented technology benefit from the same treatment; invent the process, then be consistent with it.
Deliberate seamlessness, such as a single cast form, is a valid choice when the object story supports it.
known_limits: Authored modelling guidance; it asserts no manufacturing standard, tolerance value or material property.
Real engineering fits, draft angles and clearances need engineering sources rather than this rule.
